title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation per task deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; discordant pairs n10 = 1, n01 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair correcting a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, failure diagnosis, artifact-grounded reproducibility guidance, and bounded limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness in such workflows depends on produced configurations satisfying deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering/workflow constraints, and safety-group constraints). Prior work prototypes intent→configuration translation and advocates verifier-integrated pipelines, but there is limited artifact-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal impact of verifier-triggered repairs under a tightly controlled design [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measures the marginal effect of permitting at most one automated verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under these semantics the experiment isolates a repair-only estimand: baseline and guarded episodes begin from exactly the same sampled initial generation per task, so any paired outcome difference can arise only from deterministic validation and the optional repair. Our contributions are (1) a fully archived preregistered paired execution with deterministic reconciliation; (2) artifact-grounded confirmatory statistics and exact accounting (model_calls_used = 201; shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1); (3) a focused failure diagnosis illustrating the repaired multi-device ordering fault; and (4) a bounded interpretation of operational implications and reproducibility guidance supported by the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Intent-based network-configuration synthesis and LLM-driven NetOps prototypes have been explored in recent literature, which demonstrates prototypes and benchmark-style evaluations but limited verifier-backed acceptance metrics at scale [1],[3]. Work in program repair and test-in-the-loop pipelines shows that generate→validate→repair patterns can materially improve correctness in software domains; these studies motivate guarded NetOps pipelines yet do not directly establish empirical effect sizes for network invariants [4],[5]. Surveys of agentic AI and LLM safety emphasize hallucination, misinterpretation, and the importance of verifier gates and provenance recording for operational workflows [6],[7].

Relation to our study. Prior NetOps evaluations often compare independent first-pass generations or multi-sample prompting; by contrast, our preregistered design intentionally fixes the initial generation to be shared across conditions and therefore measures only the effect of deterministic validation and the single permitted repair. This narrower estimand complements, rather than replaces, studies that evaluate constrained prompting or multi-sampling strategies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes), allowed at most one automated repair call per task, and declared one confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is archived in the execution bundle.

Task bank and deterministic sampling. Tasks (N = 200) were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and selected by a preregistered deterministic index mapping biased toward very_hard and extreme workflow patterns (multi-device ordering constraints, dependency rules). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies. Inclusion/exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks and deterministic syntactic pre-checks) were applied prior to any model calls; no tasks were excluded under those rules in the completed run. Representative task manifests and the full task_manifest.jsonl are archived.

Model configuration, generation semantics, and sampling. The execution manifest and execution/model_configuration.json declare the requested model as gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini") and record temperature = null (unset). We explicitly report that temperature = null in the archived metadata is not evidence of deterministic sampling or of temperature = 0. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one initial generation call per task was made and deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes; at most one repair call was permitted per task. The execution provider-call audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1).

Deterministic verifier and scoring. We used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the oracle. The verifier deterministically parses generated configurations, enforces per-device allowed-field constraints, required_sequence ordering constraints, group-level invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and other dependency rules encoded in each task manifest. The binary score (used for the confirmatory estimand) is full_intent_constraint_validation: score = 1 if and only if all required invariants pass. Validator traces include validation_before and validation_after snapshots, violation codes, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and a final boolean valid flag; these traces are archived per episode under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar implemented over the discordant-pair counts (n10, n01). For discordant total n = n10 + n01, the exact two-sided McNemar p-value equals the two-tailed binomial probability of observing a split at least as extreme under the null that discordant outcomes are equally likely; the analysis executor recorded p = 1.0 for the observed discordant counts. For estimation we report absolute paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) and compute a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI using 10,000 resamples with seed 1729 (these parameters are archived). Primary failed-call treatment: complete_pair_primary (include only complete pairs); a sensitivity plan treats persistent unparsable outputs as failures, but no such persistent unparsables occurred in this run.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00. Planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistency of pair accounting. Provider-call audit stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1; hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; cache_hit_count = 0.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv) reports: Baseline successes = 199, failures = 1 (success_rate = 0.995); Guarded successes = 200, failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is:

- n11 (guarded=1, baseline=1) = 199
- n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 1
- n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1) = 0
- n00 (guarded=0, baseline=0) = 0

Hence paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Statistical inference (artifact-grounded). The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test over the observed discordants (n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n = 1) yields p = 1.0 as recorded by the analysis executor (artifact analysis/results.json). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference was computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and equals [0.00, 0.015] (artifact analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg and analysis_log.jsonl). These exact numbers are archived and match the values reported above.

Repair activity and representative repaired case. The guarded pipeline triggered a single automated repair for one task (provider-call audit: repair = 1). The archived validator_trace for that pair shows the baseline initial candidate failed due to a required_sequence ordering violation: the generated sequence executed a VLAN change before ensuring the interface was administratively down in the required order. The repair prompt (archived provider trace) produced a reordered command sequence that satisfied the task's required_sequence and passed the verifier. Representative per-task artifacts and validator traces for this repaired pair are available at execution/responses/task-000008-* and execution/scoring/task-000008-*. The scoring JSON for that pair records validation_before and validation_after snapshots and confirms repair_applied = true and final valid = true.

Missingness and contamination summary. The analysis/missingness_summary.csv artifact reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero entries for unscorable or failed episodes. The analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged items (empty), indicating no detected exact token-normalized leakage between vendor-template sources and generated outputs under the preregistered contamination checks. These artifacts are archived and included in the execution bundle.
sections.discussion:
Meaning of the estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because generation_semantics was preregistered as shared_initial_candidate and exactly one initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both conditions, the observed paired difference measures the marginal effect of validation/repair applied to an identical initial candidate. It does not measure effects of constrained prompting, separate guarded first-pass prompts, or multi-sampling strategies; those estimands require independent generation semantics and separate preregistered executions.

Interpretation given high baseline pass rate. The observed baseline pass rate (199/200 = 99.5%) was substantially higher than the preregistration planning assumptions (mid-range ~45–65%), reducing realized power to detect small paired improvements. The single discordant pair produced an absolute increase of 0.5 percentage points; because discordant total n = 1, the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 under the predeclared test. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies the maximum plausible paired difference under resampling consistent with the observed data and the archived bootstrap parameters.

Operational implications and failure-mode insight. The single corrected failure was an ordering violation across devices, supporting the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering and workflow constraints concentrate failure risk. In this synthetic/deterministic environment, a single verifier-triggered repair sufficed to correct that localized sequence breach. This suggests a guarded-repair gate can be effective for sequence-conformance faults that a repair prompt can deterministically reorder; it does not generalize to other failure classes (semantic intent misinterpretation, missing external telemetry dependencies) without further evaluation.

Threats to validity and generalization. Internal validity is constrained by shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic task generation, and single-sample per pair. Construct validity is limited by the verifier's scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces encoded invariants present in task manifests but does not emulate live dataplane behaviors or telemetry. External validity is limited by the single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic task bank, and absence of adversarial contamination tests. Conclusion validity is affected by the extremely small discordant count; the discrete nature of pairwise counts leads to coarse exact-test p-values and wide relative uncertainty for small effect sizes. We report these limits explicitly and archive supporting artifacts for future meta-analyses.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that isolated the repair-only effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; the single repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.015]); exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for n10 = 1, n01 = 0. Artifact-grounded execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1), validator traces, and representative repaired-case artifacts are archived. These results support the constrained conclusion that verifier-triggered repair can deterministically fix localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting; broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-models, independent-generation contrasts, adversarial contamination, and live-device telemetry).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock; humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
